intro: A five course menu built around stone fruit at the height of summer. Peaches, plumcots, cherries and apricots run through every course, savoury and sweet, and each one uses the fruit differently: chutney, flatbread, pickle, braise and tart. The optional wine pairing adds $55.

courses.name: Peaches & Cream Tart
courses.description: Purple Haze goat cheese, peach chutney
courses.tableside: A one bite amuse to open the menu. Purple Haze is a Cypress Grove goat cheese flavoured with lavender and fennel pollen, and the peach chutney sits against it. Sets up the stone fruit theme before you describe the rest of the menu.

nuts.note: No tree nuts expected. Confirm the chutney.

vegetarian.note: No meat or fish. Confirm rennet if the guest is strict.

key_terms.definition: A fresh goat cheese from Cypress Grove in Humboldt County, California, blended with culinary lavender buds and hand-harvested fennel pollen. Named as a nod to the 1967 Jimi Hendrix song. Soft, floral and bright rather than sharp.

A category of piquant condiments from the Indian subcontinent. The word comes from the Hindi chaatna, meaning to lick. Western versions are usually sweet and sour fruit preserves, but authentic South Asian chutneys span fresh herbs, roasted lentils, raw vegetables and nuts.

sourcing.name: Cypress Grove
sourcing.description: A Humboldt County, California creamery, and the same producer whose Purple Haze appears on the Wagyu flat iron on the dinner menu.

courses.chef_notes: One bite. Introduce the stone fruit theme as this lands so the table understands the arc of the menu. Same cheese as the Wagyu flat iron, which is a nice detail if the guest has had it.

courses.name: Phoenix Suns Mottled Plumcot Flat Bread
courses.description: Basil pesto, stracciatella, prosciutto, hot honey
courses.tableside: Phoenix Suns Mottled is a named plumcot variety, and a plumcot is a plum and apricot cross. The fruit goes on a flatbread with basil pesto, stracciatella and prosciutto, finished with hot honey. Savoury, sweet and salty all at once.

dairy.note: Stracciatella. Confirm whether the pesto also contains cheese.

nuts.note: Pesto commonly contains pine nuts. Confirm this version.

vegetarian.note: Prosciutto can be left off. Confirm the pesto and stracciatella rennet.

vegan.note: Contains dairy, honey and cured pork.

key_terms.definition: A first generation hybrid stone fruit, an even cross between a plum and an apricot. Luther Burbank bred the first of them in the late nineteenth century. Entirely natural and non-GMO, created by hand cross-pollination rather than in a lab.

The soft shredded interior of burrata, made of fresh mozzarella curd torn into strands and folded through cream. Richer and looser than mozzarella, and it should be served at room temperature to taste of anything.
Honey infused with chili. The sweetness carries the heat further across the palate than a dry spice would, and it is what ties the fruit to the prosciutto here.

sourcing.name: Phoenix Suns Mottled Plumcot
sourcing.description: A named plumcot variety. Stone fruit varieties are bred for specific flavour and texture, and naming the variety rather than just saying plumcot is worth doing at the table.

courses.chef_notes: Confirm whether the basil pesto contains pine nuts, since that is the likeliest hidden allergen in this course. Prosciutto can come off for a vegetarian but the pesto and stracciatella still need checking.

pairing.wine: Szigeti, Blanc de Blancs, Burgenland, Austria, 2019
pairing.note: Austrian sparkling. The bubbles and acidity cut the stracciatella and the hot honey, and it keeps a rich savoury course from sitting heavy.

courses.name: Shrimp Cocktail
courses.description: U12 shrimp, pickled peaches, habanero-peach cocktail, lollipop kale sprouts, crispy shallot
courses.tableside: A shrimp cocktail rebuilt around peach. U12 shrimp are the large grade, poached, with pickled peaches and a habanero peach cocktail sauce in place of the usual horseradish. The habanero brings real heat, so mention it.

shellfish.note: Shrimp is the dish. Cannot be modified.

gluten.note: Crispy shallots are often dusted in flour. Confirm with the kitchen.

soy.note: Confirm the frying oil for the shallots.

key_terms.definition: Under twelve shrimp per pound. The U grade means the count is under that number, so a lower number is a larger shrimp. U12 is a substantial shrimp, and it poaches better than a smaller grade because the exterior does not overcook before the centre is done.
One of the hotter chilies in common kitchen use, with a distinctly fruity, almost apricot-like aroma underneath the heat. That fruitiness is why it works against peach rather than fighting it.
Trademarked as Lollipops and broadly known as Kalettes, a cross between Red Russian kale and Brussels sprouts. Small open rosettes with frilly leaves, milder and sweeter than either parent.

courses.chef_notes: The habanero is genuinely hot and guests do not expect heat in a shrimp cocktail, so flag it. Shellfish cannot be worked around, which makes this the course that decides whether the menu is possible for a given guest.

pairing.wine: Luli, Chardonnay, Sta. Lucia Highlands, Monterey, CA, 2024
pairing.note: Restrained California Chardonnay with enough weight for poached shrimp and enough acid to reset against the habanero.

courses.name: Cherry Braised Short Ribs
courses.description: Chestnut spaetzle, glazed carrots, cherry demi
courses.tableside: Short ribs braised with cherries, served over chestnut spaetzle with glazed carrots and a cherry demi. The chestnut in the spaetzle is worth flagging for nut allergies, since chestnuts are treated as tree nuts.

dairy.note: Spaetzle and glazed carrots are commonly finished with butter. Confirm.

nuts.note: Chestnut in the spaetzle. Chestnuts are treated as tree nuts for allergy purposes.

gluten.note: Spaetzle is a wheat flour dough.

eggs.note: Egg is structural in spaetzle dough.

key_terms.definition: A soft egg noodle from southern Germany and Austria, scraped or pressed into boiling water so the shape is irregular by nature. Egg and flour are both structural, so it cannot be made gluten free or egg free.
Treated as a tree nut for allergy purposes even though it behaves more like a starch in the kitchen. Milder and sweeter than most nuts, with a soft, floury texture rather than a crunch.
A classical French sauce built by reducing veal or beef stock with wine until it is glossy and coats a spoon. Long, slow and labour intensive, and the reason the sauce has the body it does.

courses.chef_notes: Chestnut in the spaetzle is the allergen most likely to be missed, since nothing about the dish name suggests nuts. Gluten and egg are both structural in the spaetzle and neither can be removed.

pairing.wine: Schwartz, Shiraz, Nitschke Block, Barossa Valley, Australia, 2020
pairing.note: Barossa Shiraz has the density for a braise and the dark fruit runs alongside the cherry rather than competing with it.

courses.name: Plum Galette
courses.description: Candied orange walnuts, apricot kernel ice cream, Goldberry Hill honey, cherry compote
courses.tableside: A free-form plum tart with candied orange walnuts, apricot kernel ice cream, Goldberry Hill honey and cherry compote. Walnuts are on the plate, and the ice cream is made from apricot kernels, which taste of almond. Both are worth naming for a nut allergy table.

nuts.note: Candied walnuts. The apricot kernel ice cream is a stone fruit seed rather than a tree nut, but it tastes of almond and some nut allergic guests react.

eggs.note: Confirm the pastry and the ice cream base.

key_terms.definition: A free-form tart baked flat on a sheet rather than in a tin, with the pastry folded roughly over the edge of the filling. Rustic by design, and the shape is the point.

The seed inside the apricot pit. It tastes intensely of almond and marzipan because it shares the same aromatic compound, and it is the basis of amaretto and much Italian pastry. Not a tree nut, but worth naming to a nut allergic guest anyway.

A small family apiary on Clifton Road in Clifton, Virginia, harvesting honey from wildflowers within a three mile radius of the property. The same honey appears on the roasted zucchiolo on the dinner menu.

sourcing.name: Goldberry Hill Farm
sourcing.description: Clifton, Virginia. A hyper-local apiary operating for over five years, roughly ten minutes from the restaurant.

courses.chef_notes: Two nut considerations in one course: walnuts are on the plate and can presumably be left off, while the apricot kernel is in the ice cream and is structural. Give a nut allergic guest both facts and let them decide.

pairing.wine: Poli, Bianco Vermouth of Vespaiola, Bassano, Veneto, Italy, NV
pairing.note: An unusual dessert pairing. Aromatic vermouth rather than a sweet wine, so it lifts the fruit without adding more sugar to an already sweet plate.
